# nullplatform_application_type (Data Source)

Provides information about an existing nullplatform Application Type

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nullplatform = {
      source = "nullplatform/nullplatform"
    }
  }
}

provider "nullplatform" {}

variable "application_type_id" {
  description = "ID of the application type"
  type        = string
}

# Look up an existing application type by its ID
data "nullplatform_application_type" "agent" {
  id = var.application_type_id
}

# The snapshot new applications of the type are created on
output "application_type_snapshot" {
  value = data.nullplatform_application_type.agent.last_snapshot_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The ID of the application type.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) What the application type is for; empty when it has no description.
- `last_snapshot_id` (String) The ID of the snapshot that holds the current `schema`. New applications are created on it.
- `name` (String) The name of the application type.
- `nrn` (String) The NRN that owns the application type. A caller outside the organization that owns the type reads its own organization here.
- `schema` (String) The JSON Schema the `attributes` of an application of this type must pass, as a JSON string with its properties in the order of the form.
- `slug` (String) The slug of the application type.
- `status` (String) `active` or `inactive`. Only an active type can be given to a new application.
- `visible_to` (Set of String) The NRNs where the application type can be used. A caller outside the organization that owns the type reads only its own.
